text: In Euclid's Proposition I.1 (constructing an equilateral triangle on a segment), the logical gap is the unjustified step that:
choices: the base segment AB can be drawn
all radii of a circle are equal
the two constructed circles actually intersect at a point
equals added to equals give equals
explanation: The gap is the assumption that the two circles intersect — no postulate guarantees it, and over the rational plane ℚ² the circles pass through each other without meeting a rational point, so I.1 fails. This exposes a missing continuity principle. The other steps are licensed by Postulate 1, Definition 15 (radii), and Common Notion 1.
